title: Duel Decks: Jace vs. Vraska: card flavor text

paragraphs.text: On the third night, the villagers destroyed their clocks. The sounds of whirring gears and chiming metal held only dread for them.
In the abstract memories of the Iquati, Jace found interesting ideas to improve upon.
"You know it to be false, but when its claws find you, what you know won't matter much at all." —Pol Jamaar, illusionist
Information travels quickly through Ravnica's network of messengers and thought agents.
What happens when it is the dream that wakes and the sleeper that fades into memory?
"It's as strong as you believe it is, and it's very convincing." —Jace Beleren
"The secret entrance should be near."
The Dimir would hire her, if only they knew where she lived. The Azorius would condemn her, if only they knew her name.
"The universe is my instrument, and the song I play upon it is one you are forbidden to hear."
"Words of power never disappear. They sleep, awaiting those with the will to rouse them."
Its hunger and ire are no less for being wrought of lies and mist.
"I am who I pretend to be."
"Is the maze itself a phantom? Or is one as real as the other? Perhaps I am as mad as the dragon." —Jace Beleren, journal
"As you inject the *viscus vitae* into the brain stem, don't let the spastic moaning bother you. It will soon become music to your ears." —Stitcher Geralf
"Everyone in this city is choosing sides. I choose inside."
"Roil tide! Roil tide! Tie yourselves down!"
"To sculpt a mind is to see every memory and thought as an individual piece that can be rearranged—or removed." —Jace Beleren
For the Azorius, the law can be a physical shield against chaos and anarchy.
Six feet of earth muffled his cries.
"Beware the seagrafs just off the shore. These waters are filled with hungry geists looking for an easy meal." —Captain Eberhart
"Heel."
"Do as I think, not as I do." —Jace Beleren
"I don't need to have the perfect plan. My foe just has to have an imperfect one." —Jace Beleren
"Brute force can sometimes kick down a locked door, but knowledge is a skeleton key."
"Is the inevitable any less miraculous?" —Veldka, wandering sage
The last reliable landmark in Tazeem just walked away.
"You can't think your way out of this, Jace. Thought implies life, and life requires a pulse—music to a hunter's ears." —Vraska
Rakdos cultists are her best customers. They never flinch at pain and are seldom good at math.
Even the lost and undead need a protector.
Every inch of Ravnica is home to something.
"Sheath your swords! Cudgels only. I see a new pair of waterproof trek boots slithering away." —Nablus, North Hada trapper
It grows to hate you.
"The Golgari would say that life comes from death and death comes from life. But sometimes, death comes from the dead." —Vraska
"Don't worry. I know the drill."
"Merciless to the point of psychosis. Let's give him a job." —Zelinas, Orzhov recruiter
Its victims feel only an itchy, wriggling feeling just under their skin. By then, it's far too late.
The Izzet's plans to exploit the undercity ran into a few stubborn obstacles.
The ohran viper is not cold-blooded. Its veins course with the same antigelid venom used to kill its prey.
Those without breath can't complain.
"Bury your dead deep. The boars are hungriest while the corpse is still warm." —Paulin, trapper of Somberwald
When civilization encroaches on nature, Zendikar encroaches back.
"Tonight, madam, it's your money *and* your life."
"You can't protect them all, Jace." —Vraska
"The Golgari expand, yes, but I refuse to call their tainted creations 'growth.'" —Niszka, Selesnya evangel
Linger on death's door and risk being invited in.
"I have seen things that would reduce a weaker person to blubbering and raving. Want to hear about them?" —Vraska
Gorgons crave beautiful things: gems, exquisite amulets, the alabaster corpses of the petrified dead . . .
"Romanticize it, glamorize it, call it what you will. To me, it will always be carnal, bloody murder." —Ayli, Kamsa cleric
If you're looking for it, it's available. The question is how much you're willing to pay.
"You are correct. This is going to hurt." —Vraska
"Watch people flock to a murder scene. Then tell me we're not all a little sick in the head." —Juri, proprietor of the Juri Revue
Enter those who are starving and sick. You are welcome among the Swarm when the rest of Ravnica rejects you.
Rumors quickly spread among thieves about a labyrinth without walls and a prize beyond all measures of worth.
